newsitem.title: USA: Commonwealth Electric restores all transmission.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth Electric restores all transmission.

text.p: Commonwealth Electric, a unit of Commonwealth Energy Systems, said Thursday it restored service to all of its transmission lines following this week's crippling snowstorm.
"We brought all of the lines up late yesterday," a spokesman said.
The utility lost three of its four transmission lines to Massachusetts' south shore communities during the blizzard of '97 on Tuesday.
Despite bringing back its main high-voltage lines, a spokeswoman for the utility said some 13,000 customers on Cape Cod and Martha's Vineyard were still without power Thursday morning.
They hoped to have all service restored by Friday, she said.
Boston Edison also reported some 2,000 customers without power Thursday.

Massachusetts Electric, a subsidiary of New England Electric Systems reported just under 900 customers without power and Northeast Utilities, which serves Connecticut and Western Massachusetts, reported 8,000 still customers out.
Parts of New England, especially eastern Massachusetts, were still trying to dig out from the storm which struck on Monday and Tuesday and dumped up to three feet of heavy, wet snow on the region.

Boston's Logan International Airport, which was closed for almost 24 hours and working with just one runway for another 12, reported Thursday morning that it had three of its four runways operational.
Many schools in Massachusetts and several in northern Rhode Island remained closed for a third day.
